'''Susan Randi Wessler''' (born 1953, in [[New York City]]), <small>[[Foreign Member of the Royal Society|ForMemRS]]</small>, is an American plant [[molecular biologist]] and [[geneticist]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.plantbio.uga.edu/~suew/ |title=UGA Plant Biology Department Biography of Wessler |website=plantbio.uga.edu |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20060901073536/http://www.plantbio.uga.edu/~suew/ |archivedate=2006-09-01 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.genetics.uga.edu/people_bio_wessler.html |title=UGA Genetics Adjunct Faculty biography of wessler |website=genetics.uga.edu |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20060901151311/http://www.genetics.uga.edu/people_bio_wessler.html |archivedate=2006-09-01 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nasonline.org/site/PageServer?pagename=INTERVIEWS_Susan_Wessler |title=National Academy of Sciences interview with Susan Wessler |website=nasonline.org |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20060528154417/http://www.nasonline.org/site/PageServer?pagename=INTERVIEWS_Susan_Wessler |archivedate=2006-05-28 }}</ref> She is distinguished professor of genetics at the [[University of California, Riverside|University of California, Riverside (UCR)]].<ref name=scopus>{{Scopus id}}</ref><ref name=science1>{{Cite journal|last1=Tuskan|first1=G. A.|last2=Difazio|first2=S.|last3=Jansson|first3=S.|last4=Bohlmann|first4=J.|last5=Grigoriev|first5=I.|last6=Hellsten|first6=U.|last7=Putnam|first7=N.|last8=Ralph|first8=S.|last9=Rombauts|first9=S.|date=2006|title=The genome of black cottonwood, Populus trichocarpa (Torr. & Gray)|url=https://escholarship.org/content/qt3101x2rn/qt3101x2rn.pdf?t=li5dgw|journal=[[Science (journal)|Science]]|volume=313|issue=5793|pages=1596–1604|doi=10.1126/science.1128691|issn=1095-9203|pmid=16973872|bibcode=2006Sci...313.1596T|osti=901819 |s2cid=7717980}} {{subscription required}}</ref><ref name=science2>{{Cite journal|author1-link=Patrick Schnable|last1=Schnable|first1=Patrick S.|last2=Ware|first2=Doreen|last3=Fulton|first3=Robert S.|last4=Stein|first4=Joshua C.|last5=Wei|first5=Fusheng|last6=Pasternak|first6=Shiran|last7=Liang|first7=Chengzhi|last8=Zhang|first8=Jianwei|last9=Fulton|first9=Lucinda|date=2009|title=The B73 maize genome: complexity, diversity, and dynamics|url=https://dr.lib.iastate.edu/bitstreams/deb93473-1f37-4179-9c23-14c9efe2ec9e/download|journal=Science|volume=326|issue=5956|pages=1112–1115|doi=10.1126/science.1178534|issn=1095-9203|pmid=19965430|bibcode=2009Sci...326.1112S|s2cid=21433160}} {{subscription required}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Chen|first1=Jinfeng|last2=Wrightsman|first2=Travis R.|last3=Wessler|first3=Susan R.|last4=Stajich|first4=Jason E.|date=2017|title=RelocaTE2: a high resolution transposable element insertion site mapping tool for population resequencing|journal=[[PeerJ]]|volume=5|article-number=e2942|doi=10.7717/peerj.2942|pmc=5274521|pmid=28149701 |doi-access=free }} {{open access}}</ref>

==Education==
Wessler graduated from the [[Bronx High School of Science]] in 1970.<ref name=Alumni>"Susan R. Wessler '70 Elected Home Secretary of Prestigious national Academy of Science," ''The Bronx High School of Science Alumni News'', Summer 2011, pp. 1, 5.</ref>  She received her bachelor's degree in 1974 in [[Biology]] from the [[State University of New York at Stony Brook]] and her Ph.D. in [[Biochemistry]] from [[Cornell University]] in 1980.<ref name=Alumni />

==Career and research==
She was a [[postdoctoral research]] [[fellow]] at the [[Carnegie Institution of Washington]] in the Department of [[Embryology]] from 1980 to 1982.<ref name=Alumni /> She joined the faculty at University of Georgia (UGA) in 1983 as an assistant professor of [[botany]] becoming a full professor in 1992.<ref name=Alumni /> She was named distinguished research professor in 1994 and regents professor in 2005.<ref name=Alumni />

In 2006, Professor Wessler was named a [[Howard Hughes Medical Institute]] (HHMI) Professor.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hhmi.org/research/professors/wessler_bio.html|title=Susan Wessler at HHMI|publisher=Howard Hughes Medical Institute}}</ref><ref name=Alumni />  She is also a ''professor at large'' at the [[Keck Graduate Institute]] at the [[Claremont Colleges]] in [[Claremont, California]].<ref>
{{ cite web| url= http://www.kgi.edu/faculty-and-research/adjunct-and-visiting-faculty.html| title= Keck Graduate Institute website Adjunct Faculty page| url-status= dead| archiveurl= https://web.archive.org/web/20110602150849/http://www.kgi.edu/faculty-and-research/adjunct-and-visiting-faculty.html| archivedate= 2011-06-02}} .  Accessed June 22, 2011.</ref>

Her research<ref name=scopus/> focuses on identifying plant [[transposable elements]] and determining how they contribute to [[gene]] and [[genome]] [[evolution]].<ref name=Alumni /><ref name=science1/><ref name=science2/> Her work has deciphered how transposable elements generate genetic diversity and attain high copy numbers without killing their host.<ref name=formemrs/> Her laboratory demonstrated that elements could function as [[intron]]s and that [[retrotransposons]] are the major cause of spontaneous insertion [[mutation]]s in [[maize]]. In the [[genomics]] era her laboratory pioneered the computational analysis of transposable elements, culminating in the discovery of [[Miniature Inverted-repeat Transposable Elements|miniature inverted repeat transposable elements (MITEs)]], the element most frequently associated with plant genes.<ref name=formemrs/> As a [[Howard Hughes Medical Institute|Howard Hughes Medical Institute (HHMI)]] Professor, Wessler adapted her research program for the classroom by developing the Dynamic Genome Program where incoming freshmen experience the excitement of scientific discovery.<ref name=formemrs/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ibiology.org/genetics-and-gene-regulation/transposable-elements/|title=Susan Wessler's Seminar: "The Dynamic Genome"}}</ref>
